speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your current symptoms, could you describe the severity and location of your flank pain, and have you noticed any changes in your urine, such as blood or foul odor?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any burning or pain when urinating, or noticed any blood in your urine? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Leukocyturia: Present; Bacterial Culture: Negative; Cytospin Stained With Hansel’s Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm is highly suggestive of a parasitic infection, likely Strongyloides stercoralis, which can cause renal involvement. Can you recall if you have recently traveled to an endemic area or experienced any skin rashes or gastrointestinal symptoms? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CT

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: The binucleated cells in your urine are actually eosinophils, not parasites, which strongly suggests acute interstitial nephritis triggered by your recent antibiotic use. I need to confirm your kidney function; what were the results of your serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen tests? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Creatinine

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated creatinine and urea confirm acute kidney injury, which, combined with the fever, rash, and eosinophiluria following antibiotic exposure, strongly points to acute interstitial nephritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
